figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: One widely cited 2026 comparison put fresher machine learning engineer offers in the roughly ₹12–25 lakh range against roughly ₹8–20 lakh for data science freshers, while a separate salary tracker put the median machine learning engineer salary across all experience levels at around ₹12–13 lakh a year, with freshers who show applied LLM or GenAI project skills sometimes clearing ₹15–25 lakh at AI-first startups and Bangalore commanding a real pay premium over other cities.

visuals.alt: Key takeaways: Python and the ML Toolkit.
visuals.caption: Key points at a glance.
visuals.heading: Python and the ML Toolkit

items.text: Derivatives and gradients explain how a model actually learns through gradient descent.
Treat calculus as a later unlock, not a entry requirement.
The three areas that matter are statistics and probability, linear algebra, and calculus, and none of them require research-level depth to get started.
This is the math you will use most, day to day: understanding distributions, variance, correlation, sampling, and how to read whether a model result is genuinely meaningful or just noise.
Learn it by applying it inside pandas and scikit-learn on a real dataset, not by working through a standalone theory textbook first.

blocks.heading: Matters More Than Most Beginner Roadmaps Admit

items.text: Get comfortable with Python itself, then pandas and NumPy for cleaning and reshaping real datasets.
Learn distributions, variance, correlation, and basic hypothesis testing by running them on a dataset in pandas, not by memorising formulas in isolation.

Regression, Classification, Clustering, and Ensemble Models for Structured, Tabular Data.
Cleaning, reshaping, and manipulating datasets before any model ever sees them.
Exploring data patterns and communicating findings to people who will not read raw numbers.
Pulling and joining data from real company databases, most ML job descriptions still list this.
Neural networks for vision, text, audio, and sequence problems once tabular ML is not enough.
Hugging Face Transformers, an orchestration library, vector databases
Using pretrained models and LLMs inside real products instead of training everything from scratch.
Andrew Ng's Machine Learning Specialization (DeepLearning.AI or Coursera)
Strong for building real intuition on the math and core algorithms early. Treat it as a learning accelerator, not a line item that alone gets you an interview.
Useful proof you can build working TensorFlow models, but employers weigh a deployed project or a documented case study more heavily than the badge itself.
Generic "become a data scientist in weeks" bootcamp certificates
Wide variance in quality. If you take one, judge it by whether it forces you to build and deploy a real project, not by the certificate design.
University-run PG diplomas or certifications in AI/ML

Can help with peer accountability, mentorship, and sometimes placement access, especially if you are self-taught with no existing network. The credential itself still will not replace a portfolio in an interview.

visuals.alt: Checklist: Kaggle Vs a Real Portfolio.
visuals.caption: Questions to use before deciding.
visuals.heading: Kaggle Vs a Real Portfolio

items.text: Kaggle hands you the data, the problem, and the metric already defined.
Aim for three to five real, end-to-end projects instead of a long list of small notebooks.
Document each project properly on GitHub: the problem you chose, the options you considered, why you picked the approach you did, and what you would measure to know it worked.
Deploy at least one project somewhere real, even a small hosted API or a simple web app.
Get one honest outside review from someone already working in ML before you lean on a portfolio nobody else has stress-tested.
